Design evidence for
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-foundation-concern-contribution-contract.md
section 11, gate point 8. DESIGN ONLY -- nothing consumes this yet.
## Two directions, and why both
The generic path must reproduce every legacy case (none may be lost) AND
must add the cases the dialect could not express (or it has reproduced the
dialect rather than replaced it). A one-directional map would let either
half slip: a shrinking count reads as cleanup, a growing one as progress.
## The 53 are a COUNT here, not a list, and that is a stated gap
Platform's inventory (d7b8ca6a) holds the rows: 33 verifier, 14 builder,
6 type-boundary. They live in Platform's repository and are NOT restated
here -- a copy would be a second authority that drifts. `legacy_total` is
the number this map is accountable to; the Platform lane owns the
row-by-row mapping and must supply it before the parity gate can pass.
## Why the legacy count cannot simply be matched
The dialect collapses provider, binding and verification into ONE
declaration plus an import probe. Shapes it cannot STATE it cannot TEST,
so nine cases below have no legacy counterpart by construction. Passing 53
and adding none of them would mean the generic path reproduced the dialect.
## The gate, not merely the debt
`parity_gate_passed` is FALSE and deleting Platform's dialect requires it
TRUE. Recording the debt was not enough: the previous revision asserted
`legacy_rows_supplied_here` stays false and nothing failed if deletion
proceeded while it was. A field that records an obligation without blocking
on it is a note, not a gate.
Flipping it requires the per-row mapping of all 53 legacy cases, supplied by
the Platform lane. Until then step 5 of the migration (deleting the builder,
canonicalizer and verifier) may not proceed.
## `nonce_only` was DROPPED in revision 3
It was a case under revision 1, where a Foundation-issued nonce was the
liveness signal. Revision 3 removes the nonce entirely -- there is no
`nonce_echo` field and no nonce to echo -- so the shape cannot be
represented and the row could never fire. A provider that answers positively
while implementing nothing is now `answers_everything`, which is a real and
fireable case; keeping both would have been one defect wearing two names,
and the ratchet would have frozen the duplicate in place.
The historical defeat is recorded in the design's section 3.0, which is
where a defeated design belongs -- not as a test case that cannot fail.
## The ratchet
`legacy_total` and the length of `added` are both fixed. A change in
either direction requires an explicit row change in this file, so a case
cannot appear or vanish as a side effect.
## Platform's row map is the join partner (74dab8a8)
Its four states sum to 53, which is the number this file is accountable to,
so the two halves now reconcile arithmetically rather than by assertion.
The five UNMAPPED rows are all envelope-level and had no successor code at
all: `missing` is per-concern, and N17's 'name the highest stage actually
attained' makes 13x`missing` unrepresentable for a document never read. The
contract's section 3A.1 adds an envelope stage to close them.
## Two added cases are NOT new, and saying so keeps the list honest
`foreign_inventory` and `unknown_key` have legacy counterparts. They are
still required -- a case with a counterpart still has to be reproduced -- but
counting them as gains would overstate what the successor adds.
`added_new_total` is the honest number; `added_total` is the obligation.

added.absent_from_dialect_because: an import probe cannot observe outcomes at all
added.requires: the battery runs and EVERY outcome is negative (broken_shut)

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dual of all-negative; needs Foundation-defined negative scenarios, which the dialect has none of
added.requires: positive scenarios pass AND negative scenarios also 'pass'

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dialect accepts a locally computed digest, so this is the shape it institutionalises
added.requires: an inventory digest supplied by the caller rather than computed by Foundation over typed entries

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dialect has no injection site and no provider artifact identity to compare, so 'right site, wrong provenance' is not expressible
added.requires: an object at the DECLARED injection site whose artifact identity is not the resolved provider's

added.absent_from_dialect_because: V1 cannot bind retirement at all and now refuses it; the dialect discards it
added.requires: displacement and terminal retirement survive encode->digest->decode and bind back to the replacing assembly and provider

added.absent_from_dialect_because: Platform's dialect collapses provider/binding/verification into one declaration, so an unwired provider is not expressible
added.requires: provider resolves, no consumer binding joins it
any document carries a key outside the closed set, on DECODE

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dialect's identities are module-scoped, so the case cannot arise in it
added.requires: a verification joins a binding from a different assembly

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dialect's identities are module-scoped; a re-composed assembly at the same artifact is indistinguishable in it
added.requires: a verification naming a composition_digest other than the binding's, with the SAME assembly artifact

added.absent_from_dialect_because: the dialect has no injection site to disagree with
added.requires: an object is present at a site other than the declared typed injection site

platform_row_map.row_identity: PCP-<surface>-<ordinal>, allocated once and NEVER reused
platform_row_map.row_identity_note: A retired row SPENDS its ordinal. Reuse would silently re-point a foreign reference at a different property, which is the one failure a stable identifier exists to prevent.
platform_row_map.unmapped_resolution: All five are ENVELOPE-level and none had a successor code. The contract's section 3A.1 adds an envelope admission stage before `declared` with six refusals, which is where these five map. `document_absent` is the only verdict this programme has ever observed against a real image.
